Until then its protection is not confirmed: no local space is freed there, below it or in the folders above it, and nothing is deleted from the cloud. The other files keep being uploaded and their local space can be freed. The problem closes at the first scan that no longer finds the name.
Problem: folder kept changing during the scan

The folder {path} was replaced or removed and recreated several times while the scan walked it (an application that empties and recreates its folders, for example), so the scan could not observe it. Nothing else is affected: the rest of the Vault is catalogued and its files keep being uploaded. Until a scan observes this folder its protection is not confirmed: no local space is freed there, below it or in the folders above it, and nothing is deleted from the cloud. Changes in it are still followed in real time. The problem closes at the first scan that observes the folder.

remediation.title: Exact upload remediation
remediation.phase.upload: Nothing reached the cloud; the upload restarted and awaits verification
remediation.help: Keep copies and correct the reported condition before exact reconciliation. Cloud verification does not prove protection of the current Local Copy. No arbitrary removal is authorized; the upload restarts only when S3 proves nothing was written.
reconciliation.title: Cloud cleanup / upload reconciliation
reconciliation.help: A verified keeper remains protected when available. Reconciliation never repeats an upload that may have reached S3 and never removes different unknown content; it sends again only when S3 proves nothing was written, and never while protection is paused. Duplicate checks read exact cloud versions and may incur retrieval/egress charges.
reconciliation.reason.ambiguous_send: The provider outcome is uncertain. Keep copies, stop external S3 writers and retry once the outcome is known. The upload restarts by itself only when S3 positively proves that nothing was written.
reconciliation.reason.list_permission_de: S3 refused to list object versions or incomplete multipart uploads for this file, so reconciliation cannot see what was sent. Keep copies, grant the archive IAM identity s3:ListBucketVersions and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads, then retry.
reconciliation.reason.read_permission_de: S3 refused to read an object version of this file, so its upload cannot be confirmed. Keep copies, grant the archive IAM identity s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion, then retry.
reconciliation.reason.abort_permission_d: S3 refused to abort an incomplete multipart upload of this file; its parts are still stored. Grant the archive IAM identity s3:AbortMultipartUpload, then retry (the bucket lifecycle also reaps them after 7 days).
reconciliation.reason.write_permission_d: S3 refused to write this file although the bucket is reachable; nothing was stored. Grant the archive IAM identity s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload, then retry.
reconciliation.reason.ambiguous_receipt: Ambiguous provenance or receipts. Keep all copies; inspect exact versions using authorized S3 tools. Never choose latest by token.
reconciliation.reason.inventory_changed: Cloud inventory changed. Stop external S3 writers and keep copies before retrying reconciliation.
reconciliation.reason.identity_changed: Expected Vault/path/Source Volume or operation ownership changed. Restore the expected volume and resolve conflicting operations first.
reconciliation.reason.proof_unavailable: Make the exact version readable, explicitly recover it if it is in a cold class, check permissions and retry. This action does not automatically recover or delete unproved content.
reconciliation.reason.proof_mismatch: Contradictory independent proof. Keep copies and investigate the exact version; no permissive fallback or deletion.
reconciliation.reason.orphan_different: Unknown content differs from the verified keeper and is retained. Recover/export it with authorized S3 tools or the Recovery Kit and seek assistance. No arbitrary removal action is offered.
reconciliation.reason.cleanup_unavailabl: The verified keeper is retained but cleanup could not finish. Check provider permissions/connectivity and retry exact reconciliation. In-flight/completed deletes cannot be undone.
reconciliation.reason.keeper_missing: The exact verified keeper is unavailable. Restore access before cleanup; keep every other copy.
reconciliation.reason.markers_present: Delete markers are retained: replacement has no consent to remove them. Reconcile explicitly using authorized S3 tools.
reconciliation.reason.retry_budget_exhau: Automatic reconciliation budget exhausted. Correct the cause and retry explicitly; consumed attempts remain in history.
reconciliation.reason.expected_evidence_: Independent expected-content evidence is missing. Keep copies: a remote checksum or the current Local Copy cannot replace it.
reconciliation.reason.target_superseded: The exact version was superseded or purged. It is not revived as keeper; retain and consult history.
reconciliation.reason.target_unavailable: The exact version is unavailable. Restore access without choosing another version or uploading the file again.
reconciliation.reason.vault_suspended: The Vault is paused, needs reconnecting or has stopped protection. No reconciliation is admitted until its state permits it.
reconciliation.reason.source_volume_unav: The expected Source Volume is unavailable or untrustworthy. Restore it before exact reconciliation.
reconciliation.reason.protection_paused: Automatic protection is paused or this path is excluded. Resume protection first: reconciliation will not start an upload while it is paused.
reconciliation.reason.active_operation: Another operation owns this file. Reconciliation waits without creating competing work.
reconciliation.reason.pending_deletion: Deletion is already planned for this file. Reconciliation does not alter that consent or its targets.
reconciliation.reason.cloud_only_conflic: There is a Cloud-only Conflict. Resolve it through the dedicated workflow before reconciliation.
reconciliation.reason.already_resolved: Nothing to reconcile: this upload has already been resolved.
reconciliation.reason.owner_cancelled: The Owner cancelled reconciliation. This target remains excluded from automation.
reconciliation.reason.transient: Temporary failure. The next attempt uses the same exact version and durable budget.
reconciliation.reason.operation_failed: Reconciliation failed and is blocked. Keep copies, correct the cause and retry exact reconciliation.

folder_settings.plan_help: One plan applies to the whole Vault. Changing it never deletes cloud content or moves files immediately.
folder_settings.plan_standard_only_help: Stay in Standard: immediate access without retrieval fees; highest storage cost.
folder_settings.plan_economical_help: Standard-IA at day 30, Glacier Instant Retrieval at day 90: immediate access with lower storage cost, retrieval fees and 30/90-day minimum billing.
folder_settings.plan_archive_tiered_help: Standard-IA at day 30, Glacier Instant Retrieval at day 90, Deep Archive at day 365: progressively cheaper storage; after day 365 recovery takes hours and has retrieval fees and 180-day minimum billing.
folder_settings.plan_deep_archive_early_: Deep Archive at day 0 (next AWS lifecycle evaluation): lowest storage cost, recovery in hours with retrieval fees; replacement or deletion before 180 days still incurs minimum storage charges.
folder_settings.plan_recent_backups_help: Glacier Instant Retrieval at day 0 (next AWS lifecycle evaluation): for rotating backups kept a few weeks, with immediate access and cheaper storage than Standard; retrieval fees apply, and deletion before 90 days still incurs minimum storage charges.
folder_settings.plan_custom_help: Ordered steps are object ages since upload, not delays between steps. IA starts at day 30; leave at least 30 days in IA and 90 in Glacier Instant Retrieval or Glacier Flexible Retrieval before a colder step. Transition and retrieval fees and minimum billing apply.
folder_settings.plan_sync_pending: Plan saved; cloud synchronization is pending and will retry during reconciliation.
folder_settings.plan_invalid: Use increasing nonnegative whole days and colder classes. IA requires day 30 and 30 days residence; Glacier Instant/Flexible Retrieval requires 90 days before a colder step. One Zone-IA cannot transition to Glacier Instant Retrieval.
folder_settings.plan_caveats: AWS applies transitions asynchronously based on object age; existing older objects may transition soon. Objects below 128 KB stay in their class by default. Early replacement can incur minimum-duration charges. There are no expiration or noncurrent-version rules; a warmer plan does not restore already cold content. One Zone-IA uses a single Availability Zone.

mirror_cleanup.summary: Delete from the cloud the files that have not been on the server for a number of days, so the cloud mirrors the server.
mirror_cleanup.warning: The cloud will no longer keep the files deleted from the server: it does not protect against accidental deletions. Suited to copies that are already backups, not to original data.

minimum_storage.title: Minimum storage duration
minimum_storage.summary: Some classes bill each version for a minimum number of days once it enters them, even if you delete it earlier: how many versions are still within that minimum, what is left to pay and when they are released.
minimum_storage.how: The minimum counts from when a version enters its class, not from its upload: with a storage plan transition it enters Deep Archive after the upload. Until FrostVault observes the entry it estimates it: upload date + the plan transition's days + 1 day, because AWS lifecycle rules run once a day.
minimum_storage.small_objects: Files under 128 KiB normally do not move to another class with lifecycle rules: they stay in Standard, without a minimum duration.

cloud_usage.title: Cloud storage and cost
cloud_usage.summary: How much this Vault takes up and costs in the cloud: FrostVault's estimate from its catalog and, for a Vault with its own bucket, what AWS measures once a day and what it bills.
cloud_usage.estimate_help: The versions in FrostVault's catalog, with a monthly cost estimated from AWS list prices.
cloud_usage.estimate_none: The catalog has no version in the cloud yet.
cloud_usage.estimate_disclaimer: Estimate from the public AWS list prices ({region}, prices of {date}), not from your AWS bill. It leaves out the overhead AWS adds per object.
cloud_usage.measured_help: Bytes and objects AWS counts in this Vault's bucket, read once a day from CloudWatch.
cloud_usage.measured_objects_unknown: AWS reported no object count for this day.
cloud_usage.measured_lag: AWS publishes these metrics once a day, about a day late: the latest changes are not in them yet. FrostVault reads them once a day.
cloud_usage.measured_objects_help: AWS counts every version, previous ones included, and the parts of unfinished multipart uploads, so the count can differ from the catalog's versions.
cloud_usage.overhead_help: Bytes AWS bills on top of the files, shown apart from the files' own size.
cloud_usage.overhead_object: Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Deep Archive and the archive tiers of Intelligent-Tiering: for every object AWS adds 32 KB of index, billed at Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive rates, and 8 KB of metadata, billed in Standard.
cloud_usage.overhead_size: Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval: an object smaller than 128 KB is billed as 128 KB; the difference is overhead.
cloud_usage.overhead_staging: Parts of a multipart upload not completed yet, billed in Standard.
cloud_usage.measured_none: No bytes in this bucket on that day.
cloud_usage.shared_bucket: This Vault uses a bucket shared with other Vaults: AWS measures the whole bucket, so only the catalog estimate is shown here.
cloud_usage.provisioning: The Vault's bucket is being created: AWS's measurement follows a day or two after it is active.
cloud_usage.pending: The first read from AWS has not run yet: FrostVault reads the metrics once a day.
cloud_usage.no_data: AWS has not published metrics for this bucket yet: for a new bucket they arrive after a day or two.
cloud_usage.access_denied: FrostVault cannot read the CloudWatch metrics: the AWS identity lacks the cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics permission. Attach the updated frostvault-buckets-policy.json; the catalog estimate stays available.
cloud_usage.failed: The last read from CloudWatch failed ({code}). FrostVault tries again within 6 hours.
cloud_usage.stale: The data shown come from the last successful read.

billed_cost.setup_link: How to set up the billing export
billed_cost.system_summary: What AWS actually billed for each Vault's bucket, read once a day from a CUR 2.0 export in the System Bucket. FrostVault never calls the Cost Explorer API, which AWS bills per request. Without the export FrostVault shows only Cost Estimates.
billed_cost.not_estimate: Amounts from the AWS bill in its currency, not estimates. Taxes and credits not tied to a bucket are not included.
billed_cost.role_shared: Installation · shared bucket of older Vaults {bucket}
billed_cost.setup_open: In the AWS console open Billing and Cost Management → Data Exports and choose Create.
billed_cost.setup_type: Export type: Standard data export. Name it, for example, frostvault.
billed_cost.setup_table: Table: CUR 2.0. Tick «Include resource IDs» (needed to recognise each Vault's bucket); time granularity: Daily.
billed_cost.setup_columns: Columns: select only the ones FrostVault reads, with their default names: line_item_resource_id, line_item_unblended_cost, line_item_net_unblended_cost, line_item_currency_code, line_item_usage_type, line_item_operation, line_item_product_code, line_item_usage_end_date, line_item_line_item_type. All columns work too, but make every daily file much larger.
billed_cost.setup_format: Compression type and file format: gzip – text/csv. File versioning: Overwrite existing data export file.
billed_cost.setup_bucket: S3 bucket: This account → Configure → select the existing bucket {bucket}, then confirm the bucket policy AWS proposes. The console replaces any bucket policy the bucket already has.
billed_cost.setup_create: Choose Create. AWS delivers the first export within 24 hours and refreshes it daily; FrostVault finds it by itself.
billed_cost.setup_policy: The bucket policy lets only the AWS billing service write into the bucket on behalf of your account; FrostVault's checks of the System Bucket keep passing with it. The AWS console replaces an existing bucket policy instead of adding to it: a System Bucket FrostVault created has none, but if you set METADATA_BACKUP_BUCKET to a bucket with its own policy, add the statement to that policy by hand. FrostVault only lists and reads the prefix (s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject).
billed_cost.setup_policy_show: Show the bucket policy AWS needs
billed_cost.setup_cost: The export is free apart from a few MB of S3 storage. With file versioning Overwrite, each daily refresh leaves a noncurrent version in the System Bucket: a lifecycle rule expiring noncurrent versions under the prefix keeps that small.

ui.vault_create.retention_lock_enable: Protect the cloud copies with a Retention Lock
ui.vault_create.retention_lock_help: It protects against stolen keys and ransomware: every version stays locked for the chosen days, and nobody using FrostVault's keys can delete it earlier, not even FrostVault. It can be chosen only now: it cannot be changed or removed later.
ui.vault_create.retention_lock_consequen: Governance mode, {count} days. Superseded or deleted files stay in the cloud, and keep being billed, until their {count} days end: FrostVault deletes them from that date, without errors. Lifecycle transitions are unchanged.
retention_lock.title: Retention Lock
retention_lock.summary: The cloud copies of this Vault are locked for a fixed number of days after they are written.
retention_lock.how: S3 Object Lock in Governance mode, with a default retention on the bucket. FrostVault never bypasses it: a version deleted, cleaned up or replaced while still locked is kept and deleted from its date, the RetainUntilDate. It protects against stolen keys and ransomware, not against the bucket's owner account.
retention_lock.delete_markers: FrostVault deletes only exact versions and never creates delete markers: the weekly audit reports a delete marker on this bucket as a Problem, because someone else deleted with the bucket's keys.

exclusions.title: Exclusions
exclusions.summary: Which files and folders the Vault does not upload automatically.
exclusions.folder_rule_help: A rule such as folder/** excludes the whole folder: scans and real-time detection stop looking inside it, and files already known there keep their last known state.
exclusions.cloud_kept: Excluding never deletes anything: copies already in the cloud stay, later changes are simply no longer uploaded.
exclusions.system_folders: System folders of an app (thumbnails, converted videos, caches): their content can be regenerated, so it usually does not need protection.
exclusions.include_help: With at least one inclusion rule, only the files it matches are uploaded automatically.
exclusions.order_note: Exclusions apply after inclusions: an inclusion rule never re-opens an excluded path.
exclusions.fixed_help: System files no Vault uploads automatically. They cannot be changed.
exclusions.confirm_remove_exclude: «{rule}» will no longer exclude anything: what it covered is uploaded automatically again.
exclusions.confirm_remove_include: «{rule}» will no longer select files: they follow the other rules, and with no inclusion rule left every file not excluded is uploaded automatically.
exclusions.remove_folder_scan: Removing a folder rule starts a full scan, so the Vault looks inside the folder again.
exclusions.preview_paths: Paths to try, one per line
exclusions.inside_banner: This folder is excluded by «{rule}», so the Vault does not observe it. The list is read from disk now: it is neither catalogued nor protected.
